newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen watching Dow.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen watching Dow.

text.p: Polish shares rose on Wednesday after a four-session fall, seen buoyed by Tuesday's surge by the Dow, and analysts said eyes might remain on Wall Street in the next two days when Polish markets are closed for holidays.
"On Thursday and Friday important macroeconomic information will be released in the U.S. so there's a chance there'll be swings from that," said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.
Analysts said Wednesday's strong U.S. first quarter GDP data portended falls there but that markets would be watching U.S. employment data due on Friday.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.5 percent to 16,546.7 points and turnover rose 30.2 percent to 188.2 million zlotys ($59.6 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 84 to three with eight stocks flat.
Analysts put support at around 15,500 points.
Analysts said a negative sign was the central bank's decision last Friday to increase mandatory reserves on zloty term deposits from April 30, with banks especially vulnerable.
Of the main market's mere three losers on Wednesday, two were banks, BRE and WBK, down 3.2 and 1.1 percent respectively.
Six stocks rose 9.7 percent or greater on Wednesday.
Analysts said Budimex, up 9.8 percent in heavy trade, was reacting to its recent profit-taking fall amid the general bullish outlook on Poland's building market this year.

Construction firms Elektromontaz Export, KPBP Bick and ailing Espebepe also rose nearly 10 percent, though analysts said the latter was benefiting from a creditor's Monday statement that there was still room for a compromise debt reduction deal before Espebepe creditors meet.
